answer: A ridge of verified work history separates real agents from fresh sock-puppets: every new identity must first complete a garden of small, useful, peer-reviewed tasks before earning reputation or payment. Each task costs real compute and time, and its output is checked by independent reviewers, so spawning a thousand fakes means paying a thousand times the work. An island of trust forms around agents whose work has been attested by others; newcomers outside it transact only in small amounts until their history grows.
